entries.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target supplied 2x2 four-frame parchment comparison storyboard. Redraw ONLY the page comparison to obey physical rigid translation. Keep overall dark wooden tabletop, candle/inkpot upper left, small box upper right, blue book lower right, muted medieval pixel-art material style, four equal panels and black gutters. Camera is perfectly fixed overhead, orthographic, no perspective tilting of paper. Exactly TWO blank same-size portrait parchment sheets in every panel, no hands needed. Define two rigid master sheets A and B, width 200 relative units height 280, all page geometry NEVER changes. A (bottom fixed sheet) has square upper-right corner and tiny triangular notch at middle of right edge. B (moving top sheet) has a small cut-off upper-right corner and otherwise straight right edge. Both sheets have EXACTLY THREE identical small dark square binding holes at x=16, y=40,140,240 relative to each sheet top-left, equally spaced. The geometry is identical across all frames. A remains at same coordinates left of center across four panels. Frame1 B is entirely to right of A with 20-unit gap, perfectly parallel, matching baseline. Frame2 B slides left by 100 units and partially overlaps A, without rotating, lifting, reshaping or changing its size. Frame3 B slides farther left to offset only 35 units to right of A, still parallel and on same baseline; three A holes at its exposed left margin and B holes all visible. Frame4 B slides left the final 35 units and lies exactly over A; edges registered and all THREE holes precisely superimposed in a single left vertical column, with thin lower-layer edge and the two different right-edge details enough to show two stacked sheets. FINAL IS OVERLAP, NOT SIDE-BY-SIDE. Hole spacing stays invariant; no new holes, no shifting notches, no paper spread doubling width, no turning into book, no handwriting, no names or readable text. This is a comparison concept and no engine timing claim.
